## Passages
RESULT [attribution]: Influence functions perform poorly in most settings. The authors attribute this to iHVP approximation error at scale, uncertain convergence during fine-tuning, and, more fundamentally, the fact that parameter change does not track behaviour change.
US [attribution]: This is independent negative evidence (alongside MAGIC's numbers) against making Hessian-based influence functions the rollback analyser for a fine-tuned detector. It supports choosing seeded batch ablations as the verdict and using attribution only as a pointer.
CORRECTION [attribution]: The key result matches the abstract (poor in most settings; iHVP approximation error, uncertain convergence, parameter change does not track behavior change). Author correction: the fourth author is 'Jun Sun', not 'Junfeng Sun'.
